tonight.headline: Your 77% is still an unset lineup, not a lead — and it has been unset for two days now.
body: Nothing has kicked off on either side. ESPN's live model reads 120.9 to 70.9 and puts you at 77%, and that 70.9 is not a weak roster. KEI returns have three empty starting slots — both wide receiver spots and the defence — while Drake London (14.0), George Pickens (14.8), Parker Washington (12.0) and the 49ers D/ST (7.4) sit on their bench. Filling those three slots is worth about 36 points to them and takes thirty seconds.
So manage this week as a coin flip, not a lead. Nothing in your own lineup should change: the two cards below are a trade and a conditional free-agent add, and neither touches who starts on Sunday.

case.label: What the 77% is actually made of
case.body: Their nine starting slots hold six players. Jaxson Dart, De'Von Achane, Cam Skattebo, Tyler Warren and Travis Etienne project 71.0 between them; the three holes are worth roughly another 36 if they fill them from their own bench. At 107 they are within a Jonathan Taylor bad night of you.

case.label: Your real exposure
case.body: Jonathan Taylor and Rashee Rice are in the same Sunday night game at Kansas City, which correlates about 33 of your projected points to one script. If Indianapolis trail early, Taylor's volume case goes with it — he averaged 12.3 fantasy points per game in losses last season and Kansas City are 6.5-point favourites with a 27.5 implied total.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: KEI returns leave the lineup unset through Sunday 11:00, in which case the 77% was real and understated. Their last activity in the log is nothing this week, which is the only evidence either way and it is weak evidence.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Lamar kicks off Sun 11:00 Mexico City — and this is the last send
doFirst.title: Send Team 13 one last time: Bhayshul Tuten for Lamar Jackson
doFirst.subtitle: Re-verified on this snapshot, not carried. Lamar is still slot 20 on their bench, Josh Allen is still their starter and is not being asked for. If there is no answer by kickoff, this retires.

case.label: Why it is still live
case.body: Checked on this file rather than assumed: Lamar Jackson is slot 20, which is bench. Josh Allen is slot 0, their starter, and the offer does not touch him. Team 13 are 0-1 and carry two quarterbacks in a one-quarterback league, which is the structural surplus STRATEGY section 7 says to hunt — Lamar scores them exactly nothing every week he sits.

case.label: Their side, which goes in the message
case.body: Their RB2 is Rachaad White at 7.6 this week and 164.6 on the season. Tuten is 10.1 and 205.2, and he led the league with seven broken tackles in Week 1. That is +2.5 to their week and +40.6 to their season, against +5.9 to your week and +30.9 to your season. Their gain is larger than yours and saying so is what gets a message read.

case.label: What it costs you
case.body: Tuten has the best bench matchup on your roster this week — Denver missed 28 tackles against Kansas City, a 29.8% rate that is the third worst since 2018, and allowed 6.3 yards per carry. You are trading him at a local high, which is the right time to trade someone and the wrong week to be wrong about it. MarShawn Lloyd becomes your only bench back.

case.label: The stop condition, which fires today
case.body: The decision log says: if both this and the Golden version are declined by Friday, the read on that manager is wrong and the offer stops rather than being sent an eighth time. Today is Friday. There is no decline on record — only silence, and silence is not a decline — so I am sending it once more rather than eight more times, with a hard end at kickoff. If Lamar plays on Sunday still on their bench, I close this EXPIRED and stop.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Team 13 acquire or start a second running back, which kills the +40.6; or they trade or drop a quarterback, which kills the surplus; or Lamar Jackson appears on a Baltimore injury report. He is not on one as of this snapshot.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only — he clears to free agency 01:00 Saturday Mexico City
doFirst.title: If the Lamar deal is dead by Saturday, add Matthew Stafford free — drop MarShawn Lloyd
doFirst.subtitle: Do not fire this today and do not claim him on waivers. At 01:00 Saturday the price drops from your season's waiver priority to nothing.

case.label: The clock, which is the whole card
case.body: Stafford is on waivers in this league until 07:00 UTC on 19 September — 01:00 Saturday in Mexico City. Claiming him before that spends a priority that never resets and drops you from 3rd of 10 to last for the season. At 01:00 Saturday he becomes a free agent and costs nothing but a roster spot. Same player, two completely different prices, eighteen hours apart.

case.label: Why you would want him
case.body: You have one quarterback. Trevor Lawrence projects 14.8 this week and 282.0 on the season; Stafford projects 17.4 and 286.4 in this league's scoring. He is also the quarterback you dropped at 07:12 on Wednesday to claim Zach Charbonnet, so this is buying back a mistake at the only price at which buying it back is not a second mistake.

case.label: Why it is a ghost and not a card
case.body: Two reasons. First, if the trade above lands you get Lamar Jackson at 20.7 and Stafford is redundant. Second, the drop has to be MarShawn Lloyd, because Charbonnet's seat is frozen by the churn rule until 22 September and every other bench place is spoken for — and Lloyd is the flex fallback if Tuten leaves in the trade. Firing both moves in the same 24 hours would empty the bench of running backs.

case.label: The order of operations
case.body: Saturday 01:00: if Team 13 have answered yes, do nothing here. If they have not answered, add Stafford and drop Lloyd, and start Stafford over Lawrence — though note Lawrence's own matchup improved this week, so that lineup call is closer than the projections make it look and is Sunday's question, not Saturday's.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Another IPADE manager claims Stafford off waivers before 01:00 Saturday, which ends it at no cost to you. Or Los Angeles put Stafford on an injury report before Monday night. Or the Lamar trade is accepted, which makes the whole card moot.

whatWentWrong.title: At 07:06 this morning you dropped the third-best kicker in football for the ninth-best
whatWentWrong.lead: Cam Little was K3 on Pro Football Network's Week 2 board. Jason Myers is K9. That seat had been held for five consecutive runs on that exact ranking, and the swap is a downgrade of six places.

case.label: What it cost and what it did not
case.body: It cost you nothing in waiver priority — Myers came in as a free agent, your waiver rank is still 3 of 10, and that part was done correctly. It costs about a point of projection a week and it spent a roster move. ESPN, for what it is worth, projects Myers 9.4 against Little's 8.1, so the ranking board and the projection disagree here and I am telling you the board's answer because the board is the one built on this week's matchup.

case.label: Why the fix is not another move
case.body: Will Reichard is K5 and Chase McLaughlin K6, both free agents here, both an upgrade on Myers by ranking and neither by ESPN's projection. Moving again would make this the third occupant of one seat inside 24 hours, which is precisely the pattern STRATEGY section 3 exists to stop. Hold Myers. The seat reopens on 22 September if you still want it.

case.label: Why Little is not comeback-able
case.body: He is on waivers here until 07:00 UTC on 20 September. Reclaiming him spends the never-reset season priority to undo a self-inflicted move — the same trap the Stafford card above is built to avoid. He is in Do-not-chase below.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Myers finishing outside the top twenty kickers in Week 2 while Little finishes top five. Then this was a real cost rather than a point, and the seat is a Tuesday question with Reichard or McLaughlin as the answer, still never with priority.

whatWentWrong.title: You still have exactly one quarterback, and he is the fifteenth-ranked one on the board
whatWentWrong.lead: Both cards above exist because of the 07:12 Wednesday transaction that sent Matthew Stafford out for Zach Charbonnet. One is the trade route out of it, the other is the free route out of it.

case.label: The position now
case.body: Trevor Lawrence, analyst rank 15, 14.8 this week, 282.0 on the season, and nobody behind him. A bye, a concussion or a Sunday-morning designation and you start nobody at quarterback. Every other team in this league except three carries a second one.

case.label: The one piece of good news
case.body: Lawrence's own week got better, not worse. Denver lost 31-10 to Kansas City and missed 28 tackles at a 29.8% rate, the third worst since 2018. Yesterday's brief graded this matchup SHAKY on 'Denver among the toughest vs QB' and today's reporting says the opposite. I am taking the new side and the tile has moved to GOOD.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Team 13 accepting the Tuten offer, which solves it with an upgrade rather than a patch. Failing that, Stafford at 01:00 Saturday. Failing both, you go into Week 3 one designation away from an empty slot and the Week 7 Jacksonville problem in STRATEGY's calendar gets worse, because Lawrence is on bye in it.

whatWentWrong.title: Zach Charbonnet is a dead bench seat and the right move is still to leave him there
whatWentWrong.lead: He is OUT with a shoulder described as indefinite, he started the season on PUP, and this league sets slot 21 to zero so there is no injured-reserve slot to park him in. He occupies a live seat at a 0.0 projection.

case.label: Why this constrains the card above
case.body: He is the obvious drop for Stafford and he is not available as one: he arrived on the 07:12 Wednesday transaction, so the seven-day churn window closes that seat until 22 September. That is the whole reason the Stafford card names MarShawn Lloyd instead, and why it is a ghost.

case.label: The case for keeping him anyway
case.body: Seattle's backfield behind Kenneth Walker III is worth stashing if the shoulder is short, and no dated return timeline from Seattle was found this run or either of the last two. The stash is a bet on a number nobody has published.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Seattle publishing a timeline longer than three weeks, or Charbonnet still carrying OUT on the Week 4 report. Either reclaims the seat on a Tuesday. Him practising or being activated closes this RIGHT.

trades.theirGainLine: Their gain is +2.5 this week and +40.6 across the season, against your +5.9 and +30.9 — bigger than yours on the season, and saying so in the message is what gets it read rather than ignored.

case.label: The structure
case.body: Team 13 start Josh Allen and keep Lamar Jackson on the bench in a one-quarterback league. Verified on this snapshot: Allen is slot 0, Lamar is slot 20. A bench quarterback in a 1QB format scores zero every week, forever. Their RB2 is Rachaad White at 164.6 for the season.

case.label: Why the odds moved from LIKELY to EVEN
case.body: This has been sent seven times with no answer. Nothing about the trade has got worse — the surplus is intact, Lamar is not on an injury report, White is still their RB2 — but a read on a manager that has produced no response seven times is a read I should mark down rather than restate. EVEN is the honest label.

case.label: Why your gain reads smaller than yesterday
case.body: Yesterday's card quoted +16.0 to you on an optimal-lineup season basis that assumed Tuten occupied your flex. On this snapshot he does not - Matthew Golden holds slot 23 and Tuten is bench - so removing him costs the starting lineup nothing and the gain is the quarterback swap alone: +5.9 this week (Lamar 20.7 against Lawrence 14.8) and +30.9 on the season (312.9 against 282.0). The trade did not get worse. The earlier number was computed from a lineup shape that is not the current one, and it is worth saying so rather than letting a smaller figure look like decay.

case.label: The honest risk
case.body: You are selling Tuten in the week his matchup is best: Denver missed 28 tackles in Week 1 and he led the league in broken tackles. If he goes for 18 on Sunday you will have traded him at the top of a one-game sample, which is the correct time to sell and will not feel like it. The deal clears the bar on a season horizon, not a one-week one.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Team 13 acquire or start a second running back; or they trade or drop a quarterback; or Lamar appears on a Baltimore injury report; or Sunday 11:00 arrives with no answer — at which point this closes EXPIRED and is not sent again.

trades.sources: ESPN · Black & Teal · Pro Football Network
trades.copyText: Hey — would you do Bhayshul Tuten for Lamar Jackson? You're carrying Lamar behind Josh Allen in a one-QB league, so he scores you nothing every week, and your RB2 is Rachaad White at about 165 for the season. Tuten is around 205 and led the NFL in broken tackles in Week 1. Straight across, it's roughly +40 to your season and +31 to mine, so you get the bigger side of it. Happy either way — just thought it was an obvious fit for both of us.

worthALook.name: T.J. Hockenson
worthALook.lead: The named replacement if the Loveland thesis breaks on Sunday, still free, and still blocked by the seat rather than by the player.

case.label: Why he is listed
case.body: 65% rostered nationally and a free agent here, with the largest ownership rise of any tight end on this wire at +0.99. This league's flex takes a tight end, so a second startable one is a genuine asset here in a way it is not in Chem — STRATEGY section 9 says exactly that.

case.label: The seat, which is the only objection
case.body: Tuten cannot be dropped while the Lamar offer is live. Charbonnet's seat is frozen until 22 September. Mayer has a live reason to stay while Bowers is missing practice. Vele arrived Wednesday. That leaves MarShawn Lloyd, and Lloyd is already the named drop on the Stafford ghost card. Two cards cannot spend the same seat.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Colston Loveland drawing fewer than four targets against Minnesota on Sunday. Two straight weeks of that is a role problem no matchup grade survives, and Hockenson becomes the answer the same evening. He is a free agent, so no priority is involved — the only cost is the seat.

worthALook.name: Tyler Allgeier
worthALook.lead: New to this list: Yahoo's Week 2 waiver column has him as the lead back in a two-man Arizona backfield, and he is free here.

case.label: The role, which is the reason
case.body: Seventeen carries and two targets against Los Angeles in Week 1, described as the lead back ahead of Jeremiah Love in a two-man backfield. That is opportunity with a name attached — the first thing STRATEGY section 4 asks for — rather than a hot week on low volume.

case.label: Why he is not a card
case.body: He projects 7.1 this week and 94.0 on the season, which is below every back you roster including Charbonnet's replacement value. In full PPR two targets a game is a floor problem. He is insurance against a Jonathan Taylor or Saquon Barkley injury, not an upgrade on anyone today.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Taylor or Barkley appearing on an injury report, or Tuten leaving in the trade above and Lloyd leaving on the Stafford card — which would leave you two backs deep. He is a free agent at 40% owned, so the cost is a seat and nothing else, but do not spend a seat on him before there is a hole.

worthALook.name: Jake Ferguson
worthALook.lead: The largest ownership anomaly on this wire — 82% rostered nationally, free here — and declined for the second run on the same unchanged reason.

case.label: The number that keeps him off the roster
case.body: He is Dallas's number three behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, with 18.6 points per game without Lamb against 8.9 with him. Lamb and Pickens are both active. Ownership is -0.65 on the day, a market walking away rather than one that has not noticed.

case.label: Why the anomaly is not the signal here
case.body: The why=OWNED band usually means a manager blundered. In this case the national number is priced off the name and the role is priced off the depth chart, and the depth chart is the more recent information.

case.label: When to act
case.body: CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens appearing on a Dallas injury report. Ferguson then becomes the best free agent in this league and the seat is his the same hour. Failing that, he stays on this list and off the roster.

doNotChase.name: Cam Little
doNotChase.lead: You dropped him six hours ago. Do not claim him back — that is the single most expensive move available to you this week.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: His status is WAIVERS until 07:00 UTC on 20 September. A claim spends waiver priority that never resets in this league and drops you from 3rd of 10 to last for the season. The player you would be buying is worth roughly one projected point a week more than the one you have.

case.label: What it would actually be
case.body: Spending a season-long asset to undo a move made this morning. STRATEGY section 6 names streamers as the thing priority is never spent on, and this would be spending it on a streamer you already owned.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing involving waivers. If he clears unclaimed at 01:00 Sunday Mexico City and becomes a free agent, the comparison reopens at zero cost — but by then his Week 2 game has kicked off, so it is a Week 3 question and the churn rule still closes that seat until 22 September.

doNotChase.name: Matthew Stafford
doNotChase.lead: The right player at the wrong price for the next eighteen hours. This row exists so the card above is not misread as 'claim Stafford'.

case.label: The number that kills it today
case.body: WAIVERS until 07:00 UTC on 19 September. Claiming him now costs the season's waiver priority for a quarterback who is +2.6 on Lawrence this week. At 01:00 Saturday the same player costs nothing at all.

case.label: Why the eighteen hours matter more than the player
case.body: IPADE priority never resets. It is a single trade chip, and STRATEGY says spend it only on a player who starts immediately or wins a league. A streaming-adjacent quarterback upgrade of under three points a week is neither, at any hour.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Another manager claiming him first, which ends it for free. Otherwise the answer is the ghost card above: wait for 01:00 Saturday, then add him as a free agent if the Lamar deal is dead.

doNotChase.name: Will Reichard
doNotChase.lead: He is a better kicker than the one you have and you should not add him, and both halves of that sentence are the point.

case.label: The comparison, reported because it is required
case.body: PFN's Week 2 board: Will Reichard K5, Chase McLaughlin K6, Jason Myers K9. Reichard and McLaughlin are both free agents here, so the upgrade costs no priority. ESPN's projections say the opposite — Myers 9.4, Reichard 8.5 — so the two sources disagree and the gap is under a point either way.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Your kicker seat changed hands at 07:06 this morning. Adding Reichard would make him the third occupant in twenty-four hours. STRATEGY section 3: rotating one seat through three players is the signature of optimising noise, and it names a sequence in this exact league that destroyed value that way.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: 22 September, when the seven-day churn window on that seat expires. If Myers has by then finished outside the top twenty in Week 2, take whoever is highest on the board that week — as a free agent, never as a claim.

cannotSee.label: Zach Charbonnet still has no return date, on the third consecutive run
cannotSee.body: Seattle have published nothing dated. 'Indefinite' and 'started on PUP' is all there is. A stash with no timeline is a bet, and it is holding a live bench seat at a 0.0 projection in a league with no IR slot.

cannotSee.label: Season projections are frozen, which undercuts the arithmetic in the trade card
cannotSee.body: seasonProj produced identical figures across snapshots on three consecutive days. They do differ correctly between leagues — Bo Nix reads 295.3 here and 309.6 in Chem, which is this league's scoring items being applied — so they are computed per league rather than copied. That is not the same as being updated through the season. The +40.6 and +30.9 in the trade card are August's opinion until two snapshots days apart disagree.

cannotSee.label: Three of the fourteen tiles are not researched
cannotSee.body: Loveland, MarShawn Lloyd and Charbonnet. Loveland because no Chicago report exists, Lloyd because nothing published this week addresses Green Bay's backfield split, Charbonnet because he is OUT and the grade would be meaningless. Two others — Garrett Wilson and Jason Myers — are graded off analyst boards rather than a rank of points allowed, and say so in the evidence line.
